title: Lead - IT PMO - India
jobDescription:
About Orica At Orica, it’s the power of our people that leads change and shapes our futures. Every day, all around the world, our people help mobilise vital resources essential to progress. Established in 1874, we have grown to become the world leader in mining and civil blasting with a diverse of team of more than 13,000 across the world. It’s an exciting time to join us – we are shaping the future of mining through digital and automated technologies, embracing new ways of thinking, pioneering innovation and reimagining the way we work. About the role At Orica, it's the power of our people that leads change and shapes our futures. We are looking for an experienced Lead
- IT PMO to join our global technology team and play a key role in driving governance, transparency, and delivery excellence across our enterprise technology portfolio. In this leadership role, you will work closely with senior IT leaders, project teams, and business stakeholders to ensure technology investments are aligned to business priorities, delivered through consistent governance frameworks, and supported by meaningful portfolio insights. You will influence how projects are managed across the organisation, provide strategic oversight of portfolio performance, and help drive informed decision-making at the executive level. This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of technology delivery within a global organisation while leading a team, driving continuous improvement, and making a tangible impact on business outcomes through effective portfolio governance and project delivery excellence. We're building the future of technology delivery at Orica. If you're passionate about portfolio governance, project excellence, and driving meaningful business outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. What you will be doing Lead and continuously improve IT project and portfolio governance practices across the organisation. Provide oversight of project performance, risks, issues, dependencies, and delivery outcomes. Drive consistency in project management standards, frameworks, and best practices. Partner with technology and business leaders to support effective portfolio decision-making. Develop portfolio reporting and executive dashboards that provide meaningful insights to stakeholders. Facilitate governance forums, steering committees, and portfolio review meetings. Support project managers through governance guidance and delivery assurance activities. Lead and develop a small PMO team while promoting a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. What you will bring Extensive experience within IT project delivery, portfolio management, or PMO environments. Proven experience leading PMO or portfolio governance functions. Strong understanding of project and program governance practices. Experience working with Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid delivery methodologies. Exceptional stakeholder engagement and executive communication skills. Strong analytical, reporting, and decision-support capabilities. Experience leading or mentoring PMO teams. Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related discipline. PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent project management certification will be highly regarded. What we offer As part of a truly global company, you will have the ability to grow and learn in a diverse, collaborative culture. We foster relationships and learning through connected global and local teams, promote flexible and diverse career paths and support the development of your knowledge and skills. You will be paid a competitive salary, learn from talented individuals across multiple disciplines and be able to thrive in a safe workplace within a collaborative culture. Ignite your career at a place where your distinct potential can find its home. We respect and value all Orica promotes and fosters a culture of inclusion and Equal Opportunity Employment everywhere we operate. We treat our people and applicants with fairness, dignity, and respect, getting the best of everyone’s contributions. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, nationality, age, military or veteran, marital or disability status. - IT PMO

title: Specialist - Learning
jobDescription:
About Orica At Orica, it’s the power of our people that leads change and shapes our futures. Every day, all around the world, our people help mobilise vital resources essential to progress. Established in 1874, we have grown to become the world leader in mining and civil blasting with a diverse of team of more than 13,000 across the world. It’s an exciting time to join us – we are shaping the future of mining through digital and automated technologies, embracing new ways of thinking, pioneering innovation and reimagining the way we work. About the role We are currently seeking a Specialist
- Learning to join our Manufacturing Centre in Gomia, Jharkhand . This is a highly visible role responsible for driving workforce capability, learning effectiveness and competency development across one of Orica's key manufacturing operations. Working closely with Operations, Maintenance, Technical, SHES and functional leaders, you will design, coordinate and deliver learning initiatives that strengthen workforce capability, support operational excellence and maintain compliance with statutory and safety requirements. At Orica, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact by developing the capabilities of a skilled manufacturing workforce at one of our most important production sites. This role offers the chance to work closely with operational and functional leaders, driving learning initiatives that directly influence safety, workforce performance and operational excellence. As a global organisation with a strong commitment to people development, innovation and continuous improvement, Orica provides ongoing career growth opportunities, access to world-class learning practices and the ability to contribute to building a safe, capable and future-ready workforce If you are passionate about workforce capability, learning excellence and helping people reach their full potential, we encourage you to apply and become part of Orica's journey to shape the future of manufacturing and mining solutions. What you will be doing Lead site-wide learning, training and workforce capability initiatives. Conduct learning needs analyses and partner with leaders to identify capability gaps. Develop and implement annual training plans aligned with operational and business priorities. Coordinate mandatory compliance, statutory, safety and technical training programs. Facilitate engaging learning workshops, capability-building sessions and development programs. Maintain competency matrices, training records and workforce capability frameworks. Monitor training effectiveness through assessments, feedback and performance metrics. Support employee, contractor and new starter onboarding programs. Partner with business leaders to develop technical, operational and leadership development pathways. Drive continuous improvement across learning systems, processes and delivery methods. Support succession planning and long-term workforce capability development initiatives. What you will bring Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Learning & Development, Psychology, Education, Business Administration or related discipline. Experience in Learning & Development, Training Coordination, Workforce Capability or similar roles. Experience within manufacturing, mining, chemicals, industrial operations, heavy industry or comparable environments. Strong facilitation, coaching and stakeholder engagement skills. Experience developing training plans, competency frameworks and learning programs. Ability to influence stakeholders and build strong working relationships across all levels. Excellent communication, presentation and relationship management skills. Highly regarded: Experience with Learning Management Systems (LMS) and digital learning platforms. Exposure to competency-based learning frameworks. Knowledge of statutory training requirements in industrial environments. Certification in Learning & Development, Training, Facilitation or Coaching. Experience supporting leadership development and succession planning initiatives. What we offer As part of a truly global company, you will have the ability to grow and learn in a diverse, collaborative culture. We foster relationships and learning through connected global and local teams, promote flexible and diverse career paths and support the development of your knowledge and skills. You will be paid a competitive salary, learn from talented individuals across multiple disciplines and be able to thrive in a safe workplace within a collaborative culture. Ignite your career at a place where your distinct potential can find its home. We respect and value all Orica promotes and fosters a culture of inclusion and Equal Opportunity Employment everywhere we operate. We treat our people and applicants with fairness, dignity, and respect, getting the best of everyone’s contributions. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, nationality, age, military or veteran, marital or disability status.

Strong facilitation, coaching and stakeholder engagement skills.

Ability to influence stakeholders and build strong working relationships across all levels.
Excellent communication, presentation and relationship management skills.

About the role Orica is looking for an Electrical Project Engineer to support the safe and efficient delivery of our plant projects in Gomia . This role is ideal for someone who enjoys both design work and hands‑on site execution, and wants to contribute to reliable operations in a chemical/process plant environment. You will be involved in greenfield (new build) and brownfield (plant upgrades) projects, ensuring that all electrical systems are designed, reviewed, installed, and commissioned to Orica’s standards. You’ll work with a strong engineering team, gain exposure to complex plant operations, and grow your technical and project expertise. About the role At Orica, it’s the power of our people that leads change and shapes our futures. Every day, all around the world, our people help mobilise vital resources essential to progress. We are seeking an experienced Superintendent – Maintenance Planning, Power & Distribution to join our manufacturing site in Gomia. In this role, you will lead maintenance planning activities for critical electrical infrastructure, ensuring the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of power distribution systems that support site operations. This is an opportunity to play a critical role in maintaining the infrastructure that powers a major manufacturing operation. You will lead a skilled team, contribute to reliability improvements, and help ensure safe and uninterrupted operations while developing your career within a global organisation committed to safety, innovation, and operational excellence. If you are an electrical maintenance professional looking to make a meaningful impact in a leadership role, we'd love to hear from you. What you will be doing Lead maintenance planning and scheduling activities for power and distribution assets across the site. Develop and improve preventive and predictive maintenance programs to enhance equipment reliability. Coordinate shutdown planning and execution-ready maintenance work packages. Support troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and reliability improvement initiatives for electrical equipment. Ensure compliance with electrical safety standards, statutory requirements, and company procedures. Manage maintenance documentation, SAP records, technical data, and asset history. Oversee critical spare parts planning, vendor coordination, and maintenance cost control. Lead, coach, and develop maintenance technicians while building a strong safety-focused culture. Provide technical support to operational and capital project initiatives across the site. What you will bring Essential Degree in Electrical Engineering. Experience in electrical maintenance within manufacturing, industrial, mining, chemical, metals, power, or heavy industry environments. Strong understanding of HT electrical systems, substations, transformers, switchgear, and power distribution networks. Experience in maintenance planning, work management, and reliability improvement activities. Knowledge of electrical safety standards and statutory compliance requirements. Experience using SAP or similar maintenance management systems. Preferred Exposure to 33k V and 11k V electrical systems and substation operations. Experience managing contractors, vendors, spares, and maintenance budgets. Knowledge of TPM, 5S, reliability improvement, and industrial safety practices. Established in 1874, we have grown to become the world leader in mining and civil blasting with a diverse of team of more than 13,000 across the world. It’s an exciting time to join us – we are shaping the future of mining through digital and automated technologies, embracing new ways of thinking, pioneering innovation and reimagining the way we work. About the role The Senior Engineer
- Technical Services role leads the Regional Technical Services team to deliver safe, practical and value-adding technical support to customers. It translates technical insight into measurable outcomes, strengthens customer partnerships, and contributes to sustainable revenue growth for Orica. Based at our Udaipur site, this is a customer-facing, site-based role that works closely with mining operations across the region. It also involves regular travel to customer sites to support technical delivery, build relationships and drive performance improvements on the ground. The role also builds team capability, supports business development, and ensures consistent, compliant and high-quality delivery of Technical Services across customer sites. Strong understanding of underground charging methods, initiation systems, blast design practices, sequence control and blast performance assessment. Strong safety leadership and ability to manage risk in site-based underground mining environments. Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and build trusted customer relationships. Ability to lead, influence, coach field engineers and manage competing priorities across multiple customer sites. Why this role matters This role sits at the intersection of technical excellence, safety and customer impact. You will play a critical role in helping customers improve blasting outcomes, driving safer operations and delivering measurable value on site. At Orica, Technical Services is a key differentiator. This role strengthens customer partnerships, translates technical insight into real operational improvements, and supports sustainable business growth. You will also help build Technical Services capability by developing people and improving how we deliver consistent, high-quality support across customer sites. What will help you succeed in this role You will succeed in this role if you can combine technical depth, safety discipline, customer credibility and people leadership. The strongest candidate will be someone who can confidently engage customers, explain technical recommendations clearly, and translate insights into practical, measurable improvements. What matters more is that you can demonstrate the core capabilities: safe technical judgement, blast performance thinking, customer partnership, clear communication and the ability to coach others.
